products.body_html:
Art House Productions presents
IN THE WIND
Curated by Tina Maneca

Presented as part of the A.R.T. Phase II NJEDA Program in partnership with Hudson County Parks

June 2026-November 2026
Opening Reception:
June 5th, 2026 6:00-8:00PM at The View

The largest public art initiative in Hudson County history, transforming Lincoln Park in Jersey City with artist-designed flags featuring original work by Hudson County artists. Presented in celebration of the organization’s 25th anniversary, the exhibition highlights the depth and diversity of Hudson County’s creative community.

In The Wind showcases original works by artists who live, work, or maintain studios in Hudson County. Installed around Edgewood Lake, the works are presented on flags that move with the wind, creating a dynamic, ever-changing exhibition shaped by light, motion, and the natural landscape. All flags are priced at $500 and will be available for purchase throughout the run of the installation.

In The Wind will be on view at Edgewood Lake in Lincoln Park (1 County Rd 605, Jersey City, NJ) from June through November 2026. The opening will take place during ACCESS JC Fridays on June 5, 2026, with a reception at The View from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM. For more information, visit jcfridays.com.

products.title: Creation from Destruction | September 11 - October 25 2026
products.body_html:
The Art House Gallery presents:
Creation from Destruction
Curated by Andrea McKenna
The 25th Anniversary Gallery Exhibition

Art House Productions proudly presents Creation from Destruction, a group exhibition celebrating Art House’s 25th Anniversary at the Art House Gallery from Friday, September 11 through Sunday, October 25, 2026. This exhibition is part of JC Fridays.

Opening Reception: Friday, September 11, 6:00–9:00 PM

Regular gallery hours are Saturdays and Sundays from 1:00–4:00 PM. All artwork will be available for purchase in person at 345 Marin Boulevard, Jersey City, NJ 07302, and online via the Art House Online Gallery.

ABOUT THE EXHIBITION
Art House Productions is proud to celebrate its 25th Anniversary Season. Founded in 2001 in response to the tragic events of September 11, Art House was founded as a way to help heal and connect a devastated Jersey City community through art and dialogue. Over the past twenty-five years, the organization has grown into one of the region's leading multidisciplinary arts organizations, presenting more than 270 nights of programming annually at the Art House Performing and Visual Arts Center. 

Twenty-five years later, as communities continue to navigate uncertainty, conflict, loss, and transformation, this exhibition asks artists to reflect on the enduring role of creativity as a force for resilience, connection, and hope. 

Creation from Destruction explores the transformative power of art in response to tragedy, examining how artists process experiences of grief, displacement, resilience, recovery, and renewal, revealing art's unique capacity to preserve memory, foster healing, and inspire hope.

This exhibition celebrates the strength of artists who find ways to move forward through their work. Across diverse materials, perspectives, and artistic practices, the exhibition highlights creation as an act of renewal and a testament to the human capacity to transform pain into meaning and devastation into possibility.

Participating Artists: Alex Katsenelinboigen, Alex Shammas, Alisha Garfinkel-Gross, Amy Rubinger, Andrea Morin, Anne Percoco, Beatrice M. Mady, Beth Achenbach, Cheryl Gross, Dan Peyton, Deirdre Kennedy, DISTORT, Ekaterina Vygolova, G LACORTE, Greg Brickey, Isabelle Duverger, Jada Fabrizio, Jane Sklar, Janet Jeun-Gourley, JINISTAR, Joe LaMattina, Joe Velez, Julia Kohane, Kando, Kevin McCaffrey, Lucy Rovetto, Luisa Mantelli, Mark Kurdziel, Maggie Hinders, Megan Klim, Miguel Cardenas, Miriam Jacobs, Niki Li, Patrick McCoy, Pauline Chernichaw, Peter Delman, Phil Vassil, Raisa Nosova, Robert Koch, Robert Lach, Romessa Khan, Stephanie Guillen, Susan Evans Grove, Tatyana Kazakova, Tina Maneca, and Vincent Minervini.

“This exhibition brings together artists that have shown, in my opinion, what it means to create from a place of literal and figurative destruction. This point of view not only resonates with the profound devastation of 9/11, but with how we as artists create. For me, it is often during times of ruination where I produce the work that ultimately carries me through the unexpected and devastating changes life can bring. The work I chose for this show was both painstaking and gratifying. I carefully selected each work with the belief that, in its own way, reflects the same struggle to create in the aftermath of destruction with the shared understanding that something meaningful can emerge,” says Gallery Director, Andrea McKenna

products.title: RENT: The Musical | September 24 - October 18, 2026
products.body_html:
Art House Productions presents
RENT: The Musical
Book, Music, and Lyrics by Jonathan Larson
Thursday, September 24 - Sunday, October 18, 2026

Missed out on tickets? Try your luck at the box office! We'll be selling a limited number of seats in person one hour prior to showtime, depending on availability.

Please note: We do not accept tickets purchased through third-party or resale websites. Tickets must be purchased directly through our official ticketing platform, Ludus.

Experience the groundbreaking Tony Award-winning musical and Pulitzer Prize-winning drama that defined a generation. Presented at Art House Productions during the 30th anniversary year of its original premiere, RENT follows a vibrant community of artists, musicians, and dreamers in New York City's East Village as they pursue their passions, navigate love and loss, and strive to make a meaningful impact on the world around them.

Set against the backdrop of the AIDS crisis, poverty, addiction, economic uncertainty, and a rapidly changing city, these artists discover the power of friendship, the importance of creative expression, and the enduring strength of community. Featuring iconic songs and an unforgettable rock score, RENT celebrates resilience, human connection, and the transformative role of the arts in times of hardship.

This production is especially meaningful as part of Art House Productions' 25th Anniversary Season. Founded in the wake of September 11, 2001, Art House was created to bring people together through the arts during a time of profound loss and uncertainty. Thirty years after its premiere, RENT remains as relevant, timeless, and inspiring as ever, reminding us all to measure our lives in love.

ABOUT THE ARTIST

Xinyi Zhang is a Chinese classical and contemporary dancer, choreographer, and performing artist based in New York and New Jersey. She holds a BFA in Chinese Classical Dance from Beijing Dance Academy and an MA in Dance Education from New York University, where she received the Outstanding Artistry Award. Her professional performance experience includes Limón2 and collaborations with independent choreographers and multidisciplinary artists. She has performed at venues including The Joyce Theater, Alvin Ailey Theater, and the Mark Morris Dance Center, and has participated in festivals and cross-cultural artistic projects throughout the United States. Zhang’s artistic practice explores the dialogue between Eastern movement traditions and contemporary dance. Drawing from Chinese classical aesthetics and philosophical perspectives, she combines diverse movement languages to reflect on memory, identity, transformation, and the experience of being a contemporary person.

products.title: Lizzie Borden | October 28, 2026
products.body_html:
Presented by Art House Productions, Grant Jacoby & Dancers
Lizzie Borden
Wednesday, October 28, 2026 at 7:30 PM

Not to be confused with, but still cosmically linked to, the alleged axe murderess of Fall River, Massachusetts, Lizzie Borden is an abstract love letter/ghost story dedicated to classical ballet, true crime, gay club culture, and final girls from slasher films. A lucid fever dream of overlapping shards of spectres, Lizzie Borden unfolds a strange world where failings of humankind and sexual tension blur the edges of beauty, decay, rust, and rot. Within this waking nightmare, an exploration is conducted into how we spectate, analyze, marginalize, degrade, and fetishize the human form, particularly queer bodies on stage, screen, and in society. Amidst the work’s edges and apertures, embodied trauma slides between the liminal spaces of joy and sorrow, and pleasure and pain. Dancers thrash, wait, watch, sink, seep, simmer, and splay themselves against a shifting soundscape that dares the audience to crawl inside of it and expand one’s attention span to take in movement structures and vocabulary skittering between nihilistic formalism and intimate horror.

ABOUT GRANT JACOBY
Grant Jacoby is a New Jersey-based choreographer, performer, and teacher. Originally from Wellesley, MA, he graduated Magna Cum Laude from Connecticut College with a BA in Dance and Theater and from Sarah Lawrence College where he received his MFA in Dance. A three time Boston Globe Critic's Pick, he has presented his choreography nationally and abroad in venues such as Judson Church, La MaMa Experimental Theater Club, Triskelion Arts, Movement Research, Green Space, The Mark O'Donnell Theater, The Dance Complex, Green Street Studios, Art House Productions, AS220 (Dorry Award 2016), RAW Boston (Performer of the Year 2014), Les Champs Melisey, and The International Festival of Arts & Ideas. He has had residencies at the Monira Foundation, The Dragon's Egg, mignolo arts center, SMUSH Gallery, Spoke the Hub, Dance Local, and as a part of The Shaker Dance Revival Project.  He was a company member of Quicksilver Dance and Lorraine Chapman The Company, and has performed in works by Merce Cunningham, Trisha Brown, David Parker & The Bang Group, Mark Dendy, Annie Kloppenberg, Lauren Simpson, and Audrey MacLean, among others, as well as in Ethan Stiefel & Johan Kobborg's Giselle, coached by Stiefel and Gillian Murphy, and in American Repertory Ballet's The Nutcracker. Outside of producing his own work, he also spearheaded and curated the Pop Up! Dance Series at Studio 550 and Morven Moves at Morven Museum & Garden. He has set additional choreographic work at Babson College, Endicott College, and OnStage Dance Company, and has choreographed numerous musicals including the premiere workshop and production of Friday the 13th: The Musical. He has been on faculty at Boston Ballet, The Boston Conservatory, Sarah Lawrence College, and The National Theater Institute. He is currently the Director of Marketing at The Princeton Ballet Society.

products.title: Flame (The Experience) | November 5, 2026
products.body_html:
Art House Productions & Ruby Hawk Productions presents
Flame (The Experience)
Thursday, November 5 at 7:30 pm

In 2021, Afrika Brown published “Flame”, a volume of poetry telling the story of a failed twin flame romance.

For one night, through three acts, “Flame (The Experience)” brings the poetry of the “Flame” alive through a multi-sensory journey told through sight, sound, poetry and movement that explores a failed twin flame relationship that burns to dust.

CAST
WADIAH WALIAH (Discovery)
Wadiah Waliah is an actor and writer from Newark, NJ. Theatre credits include The House of the Negro Insane, No Zooman and the Sign, Ordinary Days, The Fire This Time (standby), Slow Bullet My Three Loves, A Typical Sunday, and In Between Time. Film credits include Gazer, which premiered at Cannes. She has trained with Marishka Phillips, Charles Weldon, Arthur French, Anthony Abeson, and Petronia Paley. Wadiah is delighted to be working with Afrika again.

ALYSSA MARIE SNEED (Amour)
Alyssa Marie is a singer/actor/model based in Manhattan, New York. She recently closed a production of Beautiful: The Carole King Story with Bergen County Players and previously performed with Afrika Brown in Afrika Brown's 10 Year Retrospective, shown at The Flea Theatre. She studied her craft at The American Musical and Dramatic Academy and continued her education at The New School in Manhattan.

CRYSTAL WATFORD NUCHURCH (Aftermath)
Crystal Watford Nuchurch is an actor, producer, director, and acting coach with over 25 years in the entertainment industry. Theatre credits include The Hour, Married Single & Everything in Between, and her sold-out off-Broadway solo show Reflective Mind. Film and television credits include His Dying Wish, for which she received a Best Actress nomination, Murderous, and the upcoming series Underneath It All. Crystal is a member of SAG-AFTRA and Actors' Equity.

CREATIVE
AFRIKA BROWN
Afrika Brown is an independent playwright, screenwriter, poet, producer, and director. Her plays include The Outing, Strange Fruit Redux, A Thing of Beauty, Slow Bullet, My Three Loves, THE FIGHT, and Horizons & Higher Mountains. Her first book of poetry, Sepia Sapphire, was published in 2006. Flame, her second volume of poetry, was published in 2021. In 2025, she celebrated a decade of storytelling with a retrospective of her plays at the Flea Theater.

MEET THE FEATURED ARTISTS:

Singer-songwriter Bymaddz is a female jazz and soul singer, from New Jersey. She blends traditional with her own unique style and sound, calling her genre Cosmic Soul. Bymaddz is a powerhouse artist who vocals have been featured in the Beyoncé film: Black Is King. She’s performed for The Roots Picnic Festival and her original music has been featured in short films aired on HBO Max and The Harlem Film Festival.

DAP The Contract is a Hip-Hop and Afro-Fusion producer/rapper, classically trained pianist, and entertainment lawyer from Lagos, Nigeria and currently based in New York City. An energetic performer with palpable stage presence and 9 solo self-produced projects under his belt, DAP has performed across continents, most notably in Lagos, London, and New York, and continues to bridge worlds together with his cross-cultural understanding and genre-bending sound.

TIMALIKESMUSIC is a Brooklyn-based R&B/soul singer, producer, and multi-instrumentalist known for her blend of 90s nostalgia, musical comedy, and viral internet jingles. Steeped in neo-soul and vintage R&B, her sound pulls heavy inspiration from icons like Erykah Badu, Jill Scott, and D'Angelo. She pairs silky, nostalgic instrumentals with highly relatable, often hilarious lyrics about daily life, dating, and internet culture Her unique style and relatable humor have made her a touring sensation and a standout digital creator.

Art House Productions presents
JC Fridays
Jersey City's Free Citywide Arts Festival

In 2026, JC Fridays is expanding thanks to a significant grant from the New Jersey Economic Development Authority (NJEDA) A.R.T. Program and we’re celebrating JC Fridays’ 20th Anniversary!

What is JC Fridays?
JC Fridays is a free, quarterly arts festival that takes place in every neighborhood of Jersey City. The public is invited to explore participating businesses, galleries, bars, performance spaces, and other venues to experience visual art, live performances, screenings, talks, and creative events—while connecting with artists, residents, and visitors.
